guitar.definition: A stringed instrument usually having six strings.

violin.definition: Bowed stringed instrument that is the highest member of the violin family.

bass.definition: Having or denoting a low vocal or instrumental range.

ukulele.definition: A small guitar having four strings.

banjo.definition: A stringed instrument of the guitar family that has long neck and circular body.

mandolin.definition: A stringed instrument related to the lute, usually played with a plectrum.

viola.definition: Any of the numerous plants of the genus Viola.

double-bass.definition: The largest and lowest-pitched common member of the orchestral string family, played upright.
double-bass.exampleUsage: The double bass played the lowest notes in the ensemble.

clarinet.definition: A single-reed instrument with a straight tube.

saxophone.definition: A single-reed woodwind with a conical bore.

trumpet.definition: To proclaim on, or as if on, a trumpet.
trumpet.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "trumpet" in an educational description.

trombone.definition: A brass instrument consisting of a long tube whose length can be varied by a U-shaped slide.

harmonica.definition: A small rectangular free-reed instrument having a row of free reeds set back in air holes and played by blowing into the desired hole.

drums.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "drums" in an educational description.

snare-drum.definition: A shallow drum has tightly stretched heads and wires held against the lower head. Striking it produces a sharp, rattling sound.
snare-drum.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "snare drum" in an educational description.

bass-drum.definition: A large percussion instrument with two heads produces a deep, indefinite-pitched sound.
bass-drum.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "bass drum" in an educational description.

cymbal.definition: A percussion instrument consisting of a concave brass disk.

tambourine.definition: A shallow drum with a single drumhead and with metallic disks in the sides.

xylophone.definition: A percussion instrument with wooden bars tuned to produce a chromatic scale and with resonators.

maracas.definition: A percussion instrument consisting of a hollow gourd containing pebbles or beans.

triangle.definition: Something approximating the shape of a triangle.

piano.definition: (used chiefly as a direction or description in music) soft.

keyboard.definition: Device consisting of a set of keys on a piano or organ or typewriter or typesetting machine or computer or the like.

organ.definition: (music) an electronic simulation of a pipe organ.

synthesizer.definition: (music) an electronic instrument (usually played with a keyboard) that generates and modifies sounds electronically and can imitate a variety of other musical instruments.

melody.definition: A succession of notes forming a distinctive sequence.

rhythm.definition: The basic rhythmic unit in a piece of music.

tempo.definition: (music) the speed at which a composition is to be played.

beat.definition: The basic rhythmic unit in a piece of music.

chord.definition: To bring into consonance, harmony, or accord while making music or singing.

note.definition: A notation representing the pitch and duration of a musical sound.

rest.definition: Something left after other parts have been taken away.

scale.definition: A device that measures how heavy a person or object is.

pitch.definition: Degree of deviation from a horizontal plane.

harmony.definition: The structure of music with respect to the composition and progression of chords.

dynamics.definition: Characterized by action or forcefulness or force of personality.

music-stand.definition: A lightweight support keeps pages of written music open and visible while someone plays.

sheet-music.definition: A visual record of a musical work shows performers its notes, rhythms, volume changes, and other instructions.

metronome.definition: Clicking pendulum indicates the exact tempo of a piece of music.

tuner.definition: An electronic receiver that detects and demodulates and amplifies transmitted signals.

amplifier.definition: A device that makes an audio signal stronger.

microphone.definition: A device that changes sound into an electrical recording or signal.

speaker.definition: A box that plays sound out loud into the room.

headphones.definition: Two padded cups joined by a band, worn over the ears.

conductor's-baton.definition: A thin stick used by an orchestra or choir conductor to make musical gestures visible to performers.
conductor's-baton.exampleUsage: The conductor raised the baton before the music began.

music-book.definition: A book containing printed music, songs, exercises, or information for musicians.
music-book.exampleUsage: The student opened the music book to the next piece.
